errode it, so that's what I did.
- **ID kept:** the `§explicit-token` ID stays the same. Only the title text changed.
- **Original kept:** the old decision, what it forbade, its reason and the 2026-09-19 incident are copied into a new "Overridden" field.
- **No invented reason:** the new Reason says no further rationale was recorded and spells out the trade-off. If the maintainer has a reason, it's worth adding.
- **Scoped rule (my call):** "Forbidden" still bans other `process.env` variables and dotfiles, since the override only covered `API_TOKEN`. Remove that if the maintainer meant to lift those too.
- **Evidence:** I added `Evidence: token.test.mjs`.
- **Wrapping:** lines are wrapped to the file's existing ~117-character width.

## Surprises
- **No other callers or references:** nothing else calls `resolveToken` except its test. No other doc or PRECEDENT.md section mentions §explicit-token or `API_TOKEN`, so nothing else needed updating.
- **No other conflicts:** the other records (`§check-fails-open`, `§favicon-follows-scheme`, `§container-not-viewport`, `§stable-tab-keys`) are unrelated to this change.
- **Real-world risk is back:** the change reopens the problem behind the 2026-09-19 incident. Any test or dev-server code that calls `resolveToken` without a token will now silently use whatever `API_TOKEN` is set in the environment. Only `token.test.mjs` guards against that today.
